subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is the current source-level trajectory/session safeguard enough to close this report, or should this stay open until there is live current-main proof for the reported Windows fresh-session provider-billing path?
rationale: The inspected source shows meaningful partial mitigation, but the report has provider-independent billing evidence and the remaining failure could be in trajectory sidecars, broader session defaults, Codex/native context history, or another context-engine path.

options.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
options.body: Require a current-main Windows CLI/provider run or equivalent redacted token/context evidence before closure.

options.title: Close With Source-Only Safeguards
options.body: Close if maintainers consider the current trajectory exclusion and explicit-session-key source proof sufficient despite no live provider-billing verification.

options.title: Route To Broader Defaults Work
options.body: Treat the remaining concern as part of the broader session/context retention policy tracked by related open context-growth issues.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
recommendation.body: Require a current-main Windows CLI/provider run or equivalent redacted token/context evidence before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: The current partial safeguards and recent blame are concentrated in Vincent Koc's trajectory/session artifact commit, making this the best available owner for proof sufficiency on that path.
